references.text: The curtain of the tabernacle is described in detail in [ref:2 Mos 26:31-33|Exodus 26:31-33]. This curtain separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy. The tearing of the temple curtain when Jesus died shows that the way into God's presence is now open.
[ref:2 Mos 36:35|Exodus 36:35] describes the making of the curtain that separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy, the same curtain that tore when Jesus died.

[ref:3 Mos 16:2|Leviticus 16:2] states that only the high priest could go behind the curtain, and only on the Day of Atonement. The tearing of the curtain in half symbolizes that this restriction has been removed through Jesus' death.

[ref:Am 2:10|Amos 8:9] (correct: Amos 8:9) prophesies that the sun will go down at noon – a sign of God's judgment, which was fulfilled by the darkness that fell over the earth when Jesus hung on the cross.
[ref:Am 8:9|Amos 8:9] prophesies: "On that day I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight." This points forward to the darkness that occurred when Jesus died.
[ref:Joel 2:31|Joel 2:31] speaks of the sun being turned into darkness before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. The solar eclipse at Jesus' death can be seen as a fulfillment of this prophecy.
[ref:Matt 27:45|Matthew 27:45] is the parallel passage in Matthew, which also tells of the darkness that fell over all the land from the sixth to the ninth hour.
[ref:Matt 27:51|Matthew 27:51] is the parallel passage in Matthew that says the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom – an additional detail to Luke's account.
[ref:Mark 15:33|Mark 15:33] is Mark's parallel account of the darkness that covered all the land from the sixth to the ninth hour.
[ref:Mark 15:38|Mark 15:38] is Mark's parallel account of the temple curtain being torn in two from top to bottom.
[ref:Hebr 6:19|Hebrews 6:19] speaks of hope as an anchor for the soul, a hope that reaches inside the curtain – a clear reference to the way into God's presence being opened through Christ.
[ref:Hebr 9:3|Hebrews 9:3] mentions the second curtain that separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy, and provides context for the meaning of the tearing of the curtain.

[ref:Hebr 10:19-20|Hebrews 10:19-20] explains the theological significance of the torn curtain: We have confidence to enter the holy place by the blood of Jesus, by the new and living way he opened for us through the curtain, that is, his body.
